operativeSourceText:
(b) Section 2.05(2)(c) of the Credit Agreement is hereby
amended and restated in its entirety with the following:
(c) If, after giving effect to all mandatory prepayments of Term
Loans to the extent required by Sections 2.05(2)(a), (b) and (d), the Borrower and its Subsidiaries has (i) unrestricted cash on hand as of the last day of any calendar month in an amount that is greater than $50 million, the Borrower
shall, as soon as is reasonably practicable, but in any event no later than five (5) Business Days after the last day of such calendar month, prepay, or cause to be prepaid, an aggregate principal amount of Super-Priority Revolving Loans equal
to the lesser of (x) the aggregate principal amount of Super-Priority Revolving Loans then-outstanding and (y) the amount necessary to cause the amount of unrestricted cash on hand of the Borrower and its Subsidiaries as of the last day of
such recently ended calendar month to be less than or equal to $50 million and (ii) after giving effect to any mandatory prepayment pursuant to clause (i) above, Maintenance Liquidity as of the last day of any calendar month that is
greater than $115 million, the Borrower shall, as soon as is reasonably practicable, but in any event no later than five (5) Business Days after the last day of such calendar month, prepay, or cause to be prepaid, an aggregate principal
amount of Term Loans of any Class or Classes (in each case, as directed by the Borrower) to the extent necessary to cause Maintenance Liquidity as calculated as of the last day of such recently ended calendar month to be less than or equal to
$115 million; provided, however, if, on or prior to the date that is thirty days after the last day of the calendar month most recently ended, the Borrower obtains knowledge that Maintenance Liquidity was miscalculated for the last day of such
calendar month, and as a result, an amount that was otherwise required to be prepaid under this Section 2.05(2)(c)(ii) was not prepaid (such amount, the “Deficiency Amount”), no Default or Event of Default shall occur (or be
deemed to have occurred and be continuing) as a result of the Borrower’s failure to prepay the Deficiency Amount pursuant to this Section 2.05(2)(c)(ii) (or give notice thereof) so long as (x) the Deficiency Amount is less than
$1,300,000, and (y) within 5 Business Days of obtaining knowledge of such Deficiency Amount the Borrower makes a prepayment of such Deficiency Amount in accordance with this Section 2.05(2)(c)(ii). For the avoidance of doubt, if after any
recalculation of Maintenance Liquidity, the calculation of Maintenance Liquidity is lower than the amount most recently reported to the Administrative Agent, and therefore the mandatory prepayment that was made was higher than would have been
required at such time, the Administrative Agent shall be under no obligation to refund any overpayment amounts

findings.proposedIrEvidence: definitions[0] 'Maintenance Liquidity' with a fully-specified calculationExpression (Super-Priority RCF commitments minus (outstanding revolving loans + LC face amounts), plus 'Adjustment to Liquidity' from the most recently delivered Monthly Factoring Report, plus unrestricted cash/Cash Equivalents), citing sourceCitation '§2(b)' throughout, with sufficiency marked 'COMPLETE'
findings.verifierReasoning: The operative source text given for §2(b) only USES the term 'Maintenance Liquidity' (as a pre-existing defined term) in clause (ii); it never defines it. No retrieved context items were supplied, and Phase 2 already flagged a HIGH-severity unresolved dependency stating context could not be retrieved for an anchoring structural node - which corresponds exactly to this missing definition. Despite this, the proposed IR presents a detailed, specific multi-component formula for 'Maintenance Liquidity' (referencing 'Adjustment to Liquidity,' 'Monthly Factoring Report,' Super-Priority RCF commitments, etc.) and cites it to '§2(b)' - a citation that does not actually support this content, since the real §2(b) text supplied contains no such definition. The definition is marked sufficiency 'COMPLETE,' which is a confident claim that cannot be verified against any source text actually provided, and if the formula is wrong or incomplete, the entire capacity calculation for the Term Loan mandatory prepayment obligation (rule ir-rule:8561c2c4a1c83fdac5a1e033, which subtracts $115,000,000 from this exact metric) would be wrong. This is precisely the 'confident-but-wrong' risk pattern that deserves the highest scrutiny.

findings.verifierReasoning: The source's final sentence is a substantive risk-allocation term: it affirmatively relieves the Administrative Agent of any obligation to refund overpaid prepayment amounts caused by a later-discovered downward recalculation of Maintenance Liquidity. The proposed IR's corresponding rule carries no action, no posture value that encodes a right/permission/relief, and no capacity or comparison logic - it is effectively an empty placeholder annotated only with a description of when it 'applies.' Marking this rule's sufficiency as 'COMPLETE' overstates what has actually been captured: a future reader of the IR alone would not learn that the Administrative Agent has no refund obligation in this scenario. Materiality is uncertain because this term does not change any borrower-side capacity/basket calculation, but it is a real, independently-operative contractual protection that a competent reviewer analyzing post-closing remedies/no-recourse issues could care about, and its substance is not actually represented despite the COMPLETE claim.
